primary_sources.title: Choosing the Forcing Terms in an Inexact Newton Method
primary_sources.retrieval: Exa search; original article abstract and author PDF excerpts
primary_sources.supported_use: Inexact Newton forcing balances linear work and nonlinear progress; avoid oversolving. Does not certify the present solver.

primary_sources.title: A Flexible Inner-Outer Preconditioned GMRES Algorithm
primary_sources.supported_use: Variable preconditioning requires an appropriate flexible Krylov formulation.

primary_sources.title: KSPFGMRES official documentation
primary_sources.supported_use: Official distinction between a linear fixed preconditioner and nonlinear or changing preconditioning. The retrieved documentation version was 3.26.0.

primary_sources.title: Parallel exponential Rosenbrock methods
primary_sources.retrieval: SciSpace paper search abstract; Exa publisher-page fetch
primary_sources.supported_use: Parallel exponential Rosenbrock schemes are separately constructed methods with their own order conditions; they are not the same as solving an existing RODAS5P target in parallel. Full paper proof was not revalidated.

primary_sources.title: Rosenbrock-Krylov Methods for Large Systems of Differential Equations
primary_sources.retrieval: SciSpace search; Exa original arXiv abstract fetch
primary_sources.supported_use: Small fixed subspace order results are part of a distinct Rosenbrock-K order theory, not automatically inherited by this fixed RODAS5P method. Only abstract-level comparison was used.

primary_sources.title: Computing exp(-tau A)b with Laguerre polynomials
primary_sources.retrieval: Exa search; author university publication record and abstract
primary_sources.supported_use: Laguerre matrix-function actions motivate short recurrence and lower inner-product/storage cost. This does not prove a production bound for raw-U stage solves.

symbolic_receipt.meaning: Exact symbolic 3-stage scalar quadratic example with generic coefficients; verifies algebraic identities in that setup, not full eight-stage binary64 implementation or runtime performance.

derived_results.statement: Triangular homotopy with invertible common diagonal W has unique stages and determinant det(W)^s; exact undamped Newton determines one more stage per update, at most s updates.
If f0, J0 action and nonlinear remainder preserve a common finite-dimensional subspace and projected W is invertible, the lifted projected solution solves the original raw-U target exactly.

With valid inverse and Lipschitz bounds, E_i=kappa rho_i+sum_j<i kappa(abs(gamma Cij)+abs(h gamma)L_i abs(Aij)) E_j bounds raw-U stage error; endpoint and embedded perturbations are bounded separately.
A stable fifth-order step map plus per-step root output error O(h^6) preserves fifth-order global convergence on a fixed interval.

Fixed s,m and O(n) RHS/JVP imply O(n) state-dimension work and storage. Small common-diagonal block solve can replace O((sm)^3) dense factorization by O(m^3+s^2 m^2). No universal speedup over existing sparse/banded baselines follows.

user_assumptions: inverse L2 norm bound for W
RHS Lipschitz bounds on a valid stage domain
implementation_contract.roundoff_status: ordinary f64 estimates unless separate outward rounding and callback evaluation enclosures are implemented
implementation_contract.current_common_diagonal_solve: One m-by-m factor per reduced solve; full reduced matrix still stored; O(m^3+s^2*m^2) when s varies; at fixed s=8 an arithmetic constant improvement, not a change of asymptotic order in n or m.
